summary.summary: Chichester is debt-free — no external borrowing and a nil capital financing requirement right across the forecast to 2029/30 — and held £118.757m of investments at 31 March 2026, up £7.2m in the year. Treasury income of £6.030m beat the £4.164m budget, mainly because the council locked in higher-yielding deposits (including £51m with other local authorities) ahead of rate cuts. Its £36.8m of externally managed pooled funds have produced £12.3m of income since purchase in 2016 against a cumulative £3.2m capital loss, which sits behind the IFRS 9 statutory override until April 2029. The £13.13m directly owned commercial property portfolio produced a £640k net surplus, though voids rose to 5.4% from 2.27% a year earlier.

signals.headline: Verified quiet: debt-free (CFR nil, no external borrowing) with £118.757m of investments at 31 March 2026 and treasury income £6.030m against a £4.164m budget
signals.why: A debt-free council with rising cash balances and income well over budget carries minimal treasury credit risk.

news_drafts.headline: Chichester expects qualified audit opinion for 2025/26; clean sign-off possible 2028/29 or 2029/30
news_drafts.lead:
Chichester District Council's external auditor, which independently checks its accounts, expects to issue a qualified opinion on the 2025/26 accounts, meaning it could not fully sign them off. Draft reports for the Corporate Governance and Audit Committee on 19 October say this is "subject to completion of the remaining outstanding procedures". The qualification relates to the valuation of property, plant and equipment, the land, buildings and other long-lasting assets the council holds.

The opinion continues a recovery from the auditor giving no opinion at all for 2022/23 and 2023/24, followed by a qualified opinion for 2024/25. Property, plant and equipment stands at £156.449m, of which £137.661m is land and buildings. A further £13.132m is investment property. The auditor says gaps remain in its assurance over those valuations, over the council's reserves (money set aside) and over capital grants received in advance. Until the assets are revalued, it can give only partial assurance over them and the related reserves.

Assets last valued in 2022/23 are the sticking point. The auditor says an unqualified opinion is possible by 2028/29 only if they are revalued in 2026/27. The council's stated intention is different: "At present, the Council's intention is to have these assets revalued in 2027/28." On that timetable, the auditor's annual report puts an unqualified opinion at 2029/30.

findings.paper_title: CDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025- 26 - DRAFT October 2026
findings.headline: Chief Executive retiring March 2027 after LGR preparation; Chief Operating Officer post created to manage day-to-day operations from June 2025.
findings.detail: The Chief Executive has been focused on preparing the council for LGR and intends to retire by March 2027. A new Chief Operating Officer post was created and filled by the former Director of Corporate Services to manage day-to-day operations from June 2025. The Chair of the Corporate Governance and Audit Committee changed in May 2026, with Councillor Tim O'Kelly taking over from Councillor Richard Bates, who remains on the committee.
findings.matters: A lender assesses management stability and continuity. Significant changes in senior leadership, particularly the retirement of the Chief Executive during organisational uncertainty (LGR pause), can affect strategic execution and the reliability of financial management.
findings.figures: Chief Executive retiring March 2027; Chief Operating Officer post created June 2025; CGAC Chair changed May 2026.
findings.quote: From June 2025, the Chief Executive's role has focused on preparing the Council for LGR, with the intention to retire by March 2027. The day-to-day running of the Council became the responsibility of a new Chief Operating Officer post, which was filled by the Director of Corporate Services.

findings.paper_title: CDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025- 26 - DRAFT October 2026
findings.headline: No significant weaknesses identified in arrangements for financial sustainability, governance, or economy, efficiency and effectiveness.
findings.detail: The external auditor completed the Value for Money audit and identified no significant weaknesses in any of the three reporting criteria: financial sustainability, governance, or improving economy, efficiency and effectiveness. The audit found no risks of significant weakness in the council's arrangements and did not exercise any additional statutory reporting powers. Internal Audit received a 'Generally Achieves' rating in its external quality assessment in December 2025.
findings.matters: A lender seeks assurance that the council has effective controls, financial planning, and governance arrangements. An unqualified VFM opinion indicates the auditor is satisfied with management quality and control environment across all three strategic areas.
findings.figures: No significant weaknesses in any of three criteria; Internal Audit external quality assessment 'Generally Achieves'; no statutory powers exercised.
findings.quote: We did not identify any significant weaknesses in the Council's arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.

findings.paper_title: CDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025- 26 - DRAFT October 2026
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation decisions paused for West Sussex area on 7 September 2026.
findings.detail: The government announced a formal review of the LGR programme on 7 September 2026 following legal challenges. West Sussex, including Chichester, was one of 14 areas where a decision was paused. The council had been doing preparatory work for both potential outcomes (single unitary or two unitaries) while awaiting ministerial decision. The pause creates uncertainty around governance, staffing, transformation planning and medium-term financial planning. Local elections due May 2027 will proceed under existing council structures.
findings.matters: A lender must understand governance continuity and the reliability of forward financial plans. Uncertainty over whether the council will exist in its current form within 1–2 years affects credit assessment and the validity of the medium-term financial forecast.
findings.figures: Decisions paused in 14 areas; government review announced 7 September 2026; local elections May 2027 to proceed under existing structures; two options submitted: single unitary or two unitaries.
findings.quote: On 7 September 2026, MHCLG announced a formal review of the Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) programme following legal challenges in four county areas. The Government withdrew previously approved decisions in four areas, paused decisions in a further 14 areas and deferred decisions in two areas where outcomes remained outstanding.

findings.paper_title: CDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025- 26 - DRAFT October 2026
findings.headline: Usable reserves £119.04m at 31 March 2026, of which £30.42m not earmarked; General Fund £44.24m against minimum approved £4.00m.
findings.detail: The council holds total usable reserves of £119.04m comprising General Fund (£44.24m), Capital Grants Unapplied and Capital Receipts Reserve (£42.92m), and other earmarked reserves (£45.64m). The unearmarked balance of £30.42m provides flexibility to respond to financial pressures. The General Fund is substantially above the minimum approved level of £4.00m (20% of Net Budget Requirement). The chief financial officer reviews reserve adequacy annually and any achieved surplus is transferred to the General Fund to mitigate uncertainty.
findings.matters: A lender requires assurance that the council has adequate liquidity and financial buffers to manage in-year pressures and unexpected costs. The size and composition of reserves indicates financial resilience and the council's capacity to absorb shocks.
findings.figures: Usable reserves £119.04m; General Fund £44.24m; Capital Grants Unapplied & Receipts £42.92m; other earmarked reserves £45.64m; unearmarked reserves £30.42m; minimum approved General Fund £4.00m.
findings.quote: the Council holds significant usable reserves (£119.04 million at the end of 2025/26, of which £30.42 million is not currently earmarked for specific spend)

findings.paper_title: CDC Auditor's Annual Report 2025- 26 - DRAFT October 2026
findings.headline: 2025/26 revenue outturn £7.49m surplus, with £6.97m transferred to General Fund Reserve.
findings.detail: The council achieved a £7.49m revenue surplus in 2025/26 against a budgeted position requiring a £0.072m draw from reserves. Of this, £6.97m was transferred to the General Fund Reserve. Major contributors included £2.52m additional investment interest income, £2.00m Extended Producer Responsibility for Packaging grant not in original budget, £1.43m backdated business rates refund for Novium Museum, and £0.58m retrospective rent income, partly offset by £0.41m additional spending on temporary homeless accommodation.
findings.matters: A lender assesses financial sustainability by examining reserve trends and the council's ability to deliver budgets. This year shows significant outperformance driven by forecast improvements and non-recurring items including substantial one-off grants and property refunds.
findings.figures: Revenue surplus £7.49m; transfer to General Fund £6.97m; additional interest income £2.52m; EPR grant £2.00m; Novium business rates refund £1.43m; retrospective rent income £0.58m; B&B overspend £0.41m.
findings.quote: The Revenue Outturn showed that the Council was able to achieve a £7.49 million surplus.
